idea:
Shot 1: wide shot of a rain-soaked train platform at night, an old station clock above shows 11:58; a young woman in a yellow raincoat with short silver hair runs toward the last train.
  Shot 2: inside the empty carriage a tired conductor in his sixties with a grey moustache blocks the door and says: "Ticket's $4.50, and this train left Kyiv in 1987 — it doesn't stop for
  anyone." Shot 3: she holds up a faded paper ticket and answers: "I bought this one thirty-eight years ago. You promised you'd wait."

script.title: The 1987 Kyiv Express
script.logline: A desperate woman races through the pouring rain to board a ghostly train that left decades ago, confronting the conductor who promised to wait.
script.setting: A desolate, rain-slicked train platform at midnight beside an antiquated Soviet-era passenger train.

characters.name: Yana
characters.look: A twenty-four-year-old woman with a sharp pale face, cropped silver hair, wearing an oversized bright yellow vinyl raincoat over dark trousers.
characters.voiceDescription: Trembling clear female voice, mid-20s, faint Eastern European accent, urgent and emotional.

characters.name: Vasyl
characters.look: A sixty-five-year-old man with weathered wrinkled skin, a bushy grey moustache, wearing a dark navy railway conductor uniform with brass buttons.
characters.voiceDescription: Weary gravelly male voice, mid-60s, Eastern European accent, slow and indifferent.

shots.visual: Under a glowing vintage station clock reading 11:58, rain pours onto an empty concrete platform where Yana, in her bright yellow raincoat and short silver hair, dashes toward the passenger car door.
shots.motion: Slow pull-back as Yana sprints along the slick wet platform toward the waiting train.

shots.visual: Inside the dim, wood-paneled train vestibule, Vasyl stands firmly in the doorway with his arm raised across the frame, looking down with a stern, tired scowl at Yana standing drenched on the platform steps.
shots.motion: Slow push-in toward Vasyl as he bars the open doorway.
shots.line:
Ticket's $4.50, and this train left Kyiv in 1987 — it doesn't stop for
  anyone.
shots.speaker: Vasyl

cuts.visual: Inside the dim, wood-paneled train vestibule, Vasyl stands firmly in the doorway with his arm raised across the frame, looking down with a stern, tired scowl at Yana standing drenched on the platform steps.
Tighter on Vasyl's weathered face and bushy grey moustache under his peaked conductor cap, shaking his head wearily as he finishes speaking.

continuity.from: Yana reached the carriage door at the end of s1; now she faces Vasyl who blocks the entrance.

shots.visual: Framed past Vasyl's shoulder in the carriage doorway, Yana raises a creased, water-stained paper ticket with trembling fingers in the rain, looking up at him.
shots.motion: Slow push-in on Yana as she holds the ticket outward.
shots.line: I bought this one thirty-eight years ago. You promised you'd wait.
shots.speaker: Yana

cuts.visual: Framed past Vasyl's shoulder in the carriage doorway, Yana raises a creased, water-stained paper ticket with trembling fingers in the rain, looking up at him.
Vasyl's eyes widen in stunned silence, his jaw slackening beneath his grey moustache as he stares down at the ticket.

continuity.from: Vasyl finished speaking in s2; Yana remains at the carriage entrance and confronts him directly with her old ticket.
